html:
A Fula Muslim from Garoua in the north who became prime minister of French Cameroon in 1958 and president at independence on 1 January 1960, ruling until he resigned in 1982.

Backed by France, he crushed the UPC rebellion. After the 1961 plebiscite he led the federation of the French and British parts, then made it one party in 1966 and a unitary state in 1972. Oil from the late 1970s helped a steady economy. In 1982 he handed power to Paul Biya, but they fell out; after a failed coup by his supporters in 1984 he was sentenced to death in absence and died in exile in Dakar. See also Adamawa.
sum: A Fula Muslim from Garoua in the north who became prime minister of French Cameroon in 1958 and president at independence on 1 January 1960, ruling until he resigned in 1982.
